teaser.text: Salesforce sells online work systems that help businesses find customers, sell to them and serve them. Its business is simple to state: organizations pay for software, while Salesforce spends to deliver, improve and expand that software.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Salesforce?

paragraphs.text: The bear case assumes Salesforce’s installed base renews, but organic demand remains weak and Agentforce replenishment fails to become durable expansion. Infrastructure and selling costs rise, while debt-funded distributions restrict flexibility. The price reaches $131.27 in October 2027 and $99.30 by October 2029. Its 30% probability reflects unproven AI margins, acquisition-heavy growth and the higher debt burden, partly offset by Salesforce’s rising historical cash after stock pay.

The bull case requires production AI use to become repeatable and profitable. Credit replenishment, Data 360 and cross-selling expand contracts, acquisitions integrate well, and operating leverage funds both investment and repurchases. The price reaches $245.58 in October 2027 and $432.70 by October 2029. Its 20% probability reflects real evidence of paid use, but no consistent bridge yet from credits sold to recognized revenue, renewal and product margin.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Salesforce really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock-based compensation is another bridge between profit and cash. It reduces accounting earnings but is added back to operating cash because issuing shares is not a cash payment at that moment. Subtracting it produces an analytical “real free cash flow” measure that exposes the cost to shareholders, though it is not a GAAP category.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay today for Salesforce?

paragraphs.text: The “real” cash yield is lower because employee shares are an economic cost. They conserve cash when granted, but dilute existing owners. Salesforce may need to spend cash on repurchases to offset that dilution, so the ordinary cash-flow figure can overstate spendable owner income.

blocks.heading: What does Salesforce pay per share over time?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend rises to $1.82 in 2027 and $2.00 in 2028, then reaches $2.20. The bear case freezes it at $1.66 because the dividend has only two years of history and distributions already exceed annual cash generation. The bull case reaches $1.95, $2.30 and $2.70 as AI cash growth supports faster increases. Salesforce paid no dividend through FY24, so the base path is deliberately more confident than the short record alone would justify.

blocks.heading: Is Salesforce’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The improvement followed a painful workforce reset. Salesforce acknowledged that pandemic hiring had overshot demand, then reduced staff and office space. Free cash flow rose from $6,313 million in January 2023 to $14,402 million three years later. The improvement persisted, although the public figures do not separate savings from restructuring, stronger operations, revenue growth or collection timing.

Shareholder returns then became aggressive. In the year ended January 2026, buybacks were $12,596 million and dividends were $1,587 million. Salesforce authorised $50 billion of repurchases and issued $25 billion of senior notes to fund an accelerated share repurchase. Banks initially delivered approximately 103 million shares for cancellation. Fewer shares can lift earnings per share, but the debt creates interest and repayment obligations. The question is whether the shares were cheap enough to compensate for that loss of flexibility. The answer depends on whether Salesforce can turn its enlarged portfolio into durable customer value.

earnings.title: Salesforce earnings: December 2, 2026 results
earnings.meta_description: Salesforce's December 2, 2026 results will test FY27 guidance and whether Agentforce and Data 360 become durable, profitable revenue.
earnings.opening: Salesforce's next results are expected on December 2, 2026. Salesforce should show whether Agentforce and Data 360 turn production use into durable, profitable revenue.
earnings.closing: The full Salesforce memo also covers Salesforce's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has Salesforce guided for FY27?

paragraphs.text: Salesforce expects fiscal 2027 revenue of **$46.1–$46.4 billion**, growing **11%–12%**. It has also reaffirmed a goal of at least **$63 billion** by fiscal 2030, including Informatica and announced acquisitions.

Profit guidance also needs translation. Salesforce expects a **20.1% GAAP operating margin** and a **34.3% non-GAAP margin**. Non-GAAP removes selected expenses, but those costs remain real. Stock-based compensation is forecast at **9.0% of revenue**, and free cash flow is expected to grow only **4%–5%**. The promise therefore depends on organic sales accelerating while cash generation keeps pace.

blocks.heading: Did Salesforce keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: That issue became a governance dispute in 2026. ISS, a firm advising investors on votes, opposed adding 34 million shares to the equity plan because of the estimated value transferred through awards. Glass Lewis, another proxy adviser, supported it, and shareholders approved the proposal on May 28. Salesforce’s promises on pay have therefore improved, but the continuing test is whether AI growth creates enough value per remaining share to justify both executive rewards and employee equity.

blocks.heading: What is Salesforce's trend in the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Cash improved, but quarterly cash follows the collection cycle. The eight-quarter record is therefore more reliable than one strong or weak quarter.

blocks.heading: What should Salesforce watchers look for next?

paragraphs.text: These tests matter especially for Agentforce and Data 360, where real customer use must become durable, profitable revenue.
